stories.title: Built to Be Put Down: How Scribbi Is Reclaiming Kid-Tech from the Dopamine Engine
stories.summary: A Provo startup turned down investor money because the guy wanted them to make their kids' tablet more addictive. Instead, Scribbi's e-ink device treats a child's mistakes as data — quietly flagging patterns for parents without ever telling a kid they got it wrong.
stories.extended_summary: An investor sat across from Katarina and Keller Seamons with a simple pitch: make your kids' tablet more addictive and it'll be worth way more. They said no. That refusal is the whole point of Scribbi, the Provo startup's e-ink tablet built to be put down. When their daughter writes her S's backwards, most software would mark it wrong — Scribbi quietly flags the pattern for a parent and helps her fix it without ever telling her, in the moment, that she failed. It's a small design choice that flips the entire logic of kid-tech: a child's mistakes are information worth noticing, not noise for an algorithm to correct.
